Quick errands this morning in town... dev-c3-new, DEM and NNLC enabled.   Less right lane bias (decent lane centering) vs. FM, lateral torque good, seemed about same.    Tracked all curves incl. sharp ones well.   Turn desires response at least as good, maybe a touch better.   Two stop lights... both it almost stopped just before the line, then *very* slowly crept about 4 ft more, and remained stopped - just before I would have disengaged, and didn't.   Totally looks like a driver in a hurry.  :THONK:  First light it didn't immediately go on green though I didn't wait long (traffic) and pressed the accel to go.  Second one it promptly went on the green.   Overall so far like it better than FM and will continue driving more today.   Only objectionable behavior so far is creeping at the stop lights.  Some other recent model similarly crept, then tried to take off.   At least this one didn't do that.   Will report again after driving more on it later this morning.

In times past I found behavior of any model in this respect would vary with the weather conditions and time of day - shadows etc.   There's also the variable of the appearance of the lights themselves.   In my area most lights are suspended on cables, and a few are on posts.  Firehose was a nice jump forward, though models after that seem to have taken a step or two back in how they respond to lights - again, in my area.

That's why if I ever have the chance to fine-tune an OP model with data to intentionally overfit my area, I'll do it.    It's not a particularly large vision+policy (taken together) model and never will be on the C3X sans HW expansion, so optimizing it for region etc. makes sense.   I say this as a Tesla driver too, as the "HW3" in my car in terms of ADAS gets slowly left behind by HW4 cars now on the market.   (They appear to have run out of compute resources on HW3, so we don't get any new substantial FSD versions.)
